blocks.text: Barnston Island is a Fraser River island between Surrey (Port Kells) on the south bank and Pitt Meadows across the main channel; there is no bridge — the only access is the free Barnston Island Ferry across Parson's Channel from 104 Ave in Port Kells, a barge-and-tug provincial inland ferry, capacity 5 vehicles and 50 passengers, running on demand roughly 6:15 a.m.–11:55 p.m. (to 12:55 a.m. weekends), with crossings that can be interrupted by river traffic.
This guide covers Barnston Island's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask.
Condo buildings in Barnston Island

Barnston Island is not in the City of Surrey, despite "Surrey" mailing addresses and the "(Surrey)" framing in the candidate-area name. Most of the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A; the southeast portion is Barnston Island Indian Reserve No. 3 (Katzie First Nation). Planning, permits and taxes run through Metro Vancouver / the Province, not Surrey City Hall.
Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: Barnston Island is a Fraser River island between Surrey (Port Kells) on the south bank and Pitt Meadows across the main channel; there is no bridge — the only access is the free Barnston Island Ferry across Parson's Channel from 104 Ave in Port Kells, a barge-and-tug provincial inland ferry, capacity 5 vehicles and 50 passengers, running on demand roughly 6:15 a.m.–11:55 p.m. (to 12:55 a.m. weekends), with crossings that can be interrupted by river traffic.

The island's main road is its perimeter dike road — the dike rings the island, protects it as low Fraser River floodplain, and doubles as the transportation route; Dyke Road addresses run around it (the SD36 locator test range was 2–328 Dyke Rd).

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is no condo stock on the island in any form. The housing stock is a small number of farmhouses and rural single-detached homes on large farm parcels; Metro Vancouver's study puts the island population at roughly 150 residents, and the island has been farmed since the mid-1800s.
Schools: School District 36 (Surrey) serves the island; island children cross by ferry to their assigned Surrey schools.

Services: none on the island — no shops, recreation facilities or medical facilities; Metro Vancouver's Barnston Island Regional Park provides riverfront rest areas and protects riparian habitat. All services are in Surrey (Port Kells/Fleetwood) or Pitt Meadows, via the ferry.

Planning authority: Metro Vancouver, not a municipality: The Electoral Area A Official Community Plan (2018) sets the vision of Barnston Island as a thriving agricultural community and expressly does not apply to First Nations Reserves; Metro Vancouver — not a municipality — is the planning authority for the non-reserve lands, and also holds the zoning for Electoral Area A, including a Barnston Island zoning map (Map 12). There are no new developments of scale; the OCP direction is to keep the island agricultural.

Farm classification (BC Assessment) — stated in full three-tier form: $2,500 gross annual farm income for an operation of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation; and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" line for farm class is an error — the threshold depends on the operation's size.
Flood construction: the whole island is low Fraser River floodplain behind a perimeter dike, and Metro Vancouver publishes a Barnston Island Flood Construction Level Study.

The dike is the road. The perimeter dike doubles as the island's main transportation route, so flood infrastructure and daily driving are literally the same asset — a dike closure is also a road closure.

The island's school answer was corrected by an actual locator run (Nov 1, 2026). An earlier document-based reading pointed to Port Kells Elementary; the SD36 locator run for 52 Dyke Road returned Bothwell Elementary and École Fraser Heights for island addresses — Port Kells Elementary serves the landing side, not the island.

Services here are stitched together across jurisdictions. Fraser Valley Regional Library serves island residents under a Metro Vancouver arrangement — Metro Vancouver publishes a library-information sheet specifically for Barnston Island residents, a small sign of how services here are assembled rather than delivered by a city.

There is no bus service on the island and no bridge. The ferry is the single connection, which is why the complete absence of on-island seniors and condo services matters more here than in any mainland area: a resident who stops driving has no local fallback.

What trades here

items.t: What land actually is here: a small stock of farmhouses and rural single-detached homes on large agricultural parcels; Metro Vancouver's 2019 Agricultural Viability Study puts the island population at roughly 150 residents, the island has been farmed since the mid-1800s, and older farm-era homes dominate. Large agricultural parcels are the norm; small-lot subdivision is not the island's pattern under its agricultural OCP direction.
Fee-simple lots — the default and only documented market form on non-reserve land: a fee-simple farm parcel carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees.

ALR character: the island is predominantly farmland — Metro Vancouver's 2019 study was commissioned precisely because agriculture is the island's land base and economy. Assume ALR until proven otherwise on any parcel. Check a parcel on the ALC maps.

Floodplain character: the whole island is low Fraser River floodplain protected by a perimeter dike that is also the main transportation route; Metro Vancouver publishes a Barnston Island Flood Construction Level Study.
The island's landmarks are the ferry landing, the dike road and Barnston Island Regional Park, not complexes.

items.t: Legal geography, restated because everything else runs on it: most of the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A; the southeast portion is Barnston Island Indian Reserve No. 3 (Katzie First Nation), which is federal reserve land and not fee-simple market housing. Nearby areas: Port Kells (Surrey) at the ferry landing; Pitt Meadows across the main channel (no direct connection); Katzie's main reserve in Pitt Meadows.

Schools — settled catchment, cited as the completed run: School District 36 (Surrey) serves the island; island children cross by ferry to their assigned Surrey schools. The completed SD36 School Locator run on 2026-11-01 for the island test address 52 Dyke Road (locator range 2–328 Dyke Rd) returned Bothwell Elementary → École Fraser Heights for island homes — cited as the settled chain on its single-community basis. That result supersedes the earlier document-based suggestion that Port Kells Elementary serves island homes: Port Kells Elementary (K–7, 19076 88 Ave) serves Port Kells / landing-side addresses, not island addresses. School names are as the locator and the Ministry list returned them.
The ferry's capacity is five vehicles (Nov 1, 2026).

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Barnston Island
What acreage trades on Barnston Island: large fee-simple farm parcels under an agricultural OCP direction — the island's farm ground itself, traded parcel by parcel, if at all.
The ground in Barnston Island

items.t: Fee-simple farm parcels: A fee-simple farm parcel carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the island is predominantly farmland — Metro Vancouver's 2019 study was commissioned precisely because agriculture is the island's land base and economy. Assume ALR until proven otherwise on any parcel. Check a parcel on the ALC maps.
Bare-land strata acreage: none: No strata product of any kind was identified on the island, and on ALR parcels the form cannot be created: ALR residences cannot be stratified.
Reserve land: parcels on Barnston Island IR No. 3 are Katzie First Nation reserve lands — federal reserve land with different tenure, financing and resale rules than fee-simple lots.

blocks.text: Where the acreages are and what to know

items.t: Legal geography: Barnston Island is a Fraser River island between Surrey (Port Kells) on the south bank and Pitt Meadows across the main Fraser channel. Most of the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A; the southeast portion is Barnston Island Indian Reserve No. 3 (Katzie First Nation), which is federal reserve land and not fee-simple market housing. Mailing addresses use "Surrey," which is why the name is filed that way, but no part of the island is inside the City of Surrey.

Flood construction: the whole island is low Fraser River floodplain protected by a perimeter dike that is also the main transportation route; Metro Vancouver publishes a Barnston Island Flood Construction Level Study.

Despite the candidate-area name "Barnston Island (Surrey)," no part of the island is inside the City of Surrey — the tag is a postal convention only. A buyer who searches Surrey bylaws, Surrey taxes or Surrey servicing for an island parcel is searching the wrong government entirely.

The school answer was corrected by a completed locator run: An earlier document-based suggestion named Port Kells Elementary for island homes; the settled SD36 locator run for 52 Dyke Road (range 2–328 Dyke Rd) returned Bothwell Elementary → École Fraser Heights Secondary, and Port Kells Elementary (19076 88 Ave) serves landing-side addresses only. Any island marketing naming Port Kells Elementary for an island home is using the superseded source. (SD36 School Locator, mybaragar.com, run 2026-11-01.)

There are no services on the island at all (Nov 1, 2026): No shops, no recreation facilities (beyond Barnston Island Regional Park's riverfront rest areas and riparian habitat) and no medical facilities — every service trip is a ferry trip to Port Kells/Fleetwood or Pitt Meadows. That absence is a priced fact of island acreage, not a gap a listing should soften.

faq.q: Are there any condos on Barnston Island?
faq.a: No — none in any form. No strata product of any kind was identified on the island; the market stock is freehold farm parcels, plus Katzie IR 3 reserve land that is not market housing, and ALR residences cannot be stratified.

faq.q: Is Barnston Island part of Surrey?
faq.a: No. It uses Surrey mailing addresses, but the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A, plus the Katzie First Nation's Barnston Island IR No. 3 — services, taxes, building permits and planning run through Metro Vancouver and the Province, not Surrey City Hall.

faq.q: Can I buy a small lot and build a house on Barnston Island?
faq.a: Most of the island is agricultural land under an OCP vision of a farming community; building is tied to farm parcels and ALR rules (one principal residence to 500 m², a suite only inside it, one additional residence of 90 m² at ≤40 ha or 186 m² above 40 ha), so a parcel-by-parcel check with Metro Vancouver and the ALC is essential before assuming a building lot exists.

faq.q: How do residents get on and off the island?
faq.a: Only by the free Barnston Island Ferry from 104 Ave in Port Kells — about 5 minutes across Parson's Channel, on demand within operating hours (roughly 6:15 a.m.–11:55 p.m., to 12:55 a.m. weekends), capacity 5 vehicles and 50 passengers. It does not run all night, and crossings can be interrupted by river traffic — overnight, outside ferry hours, there is no vehicle access.

The Province, under the rural system — rural owners receive their notice from the Surveyor of Taxes and pay the Province, with a July 2 deadline, a 5% penalty on July 3 and a further 5% on November 1 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11 regime); Metro Vancouver and school levies ride on top.

faq.q: Is Barnston Island part of Surrey?
faq.a: No. It uses Surrey mailing addresses, but the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A, plus the Katzie First Nation's Barnston Island IR No. 3 — services, taxes, building permits and planning run through Metro Vancouver and the Province, not Surrey City Hall.

faq.q: Can I buy a small lot and build a house on Barnston Island?
faq.a: Most of the island is agricultural land under an OCP vision of a farming community; building is tied to farm parcels and ALR rules (one principal residence to 500 m², a suite only inside it, one additional residence of 90 m² at ≤40 ha or 186 m² above 40 ha), so a parcel-by-parcel check with Metro Vancouver and the ALC is essential before assuming a building lot exists.

faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy an "acreage" on the island?
faq.a: A large fee-simple farm parcel with a farmhouse or rural home on it, predominantly ALR ground under an agricultural OCP direction. There is no acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale acreage product — and reserve parcels (IR 3) are a different tenure entirely and are not fee-simple market housing.

faq.q: Can a suite go in a barn or a detached building?
faq.a: No — under the ALC housing rules a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence. A detached second dwelling is the "additional residence," size-capped and tied to farm use or another permitted use.

No. It uses Surrey mailing addresses, but the island is unincorporated Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A plus Katzie IR 3. Services, taxes, permits and planning run through Metro Vancouver / the Province, not Surrey City Hall — and never price it off a Surrey market figure.

faq.q: Can I buy a half duplex on Barnston Island?
faq.a: There is no strata product and no half-duplex subdivision on the island; the housing is farmhouses and rural single-detached homes on farm parcels.

faq.q: Where do island kids go to school?
faq.a: Port Kells Elementary serves landing-side addresses, not island homes.
